messages.author: 6c32846711f6e460
messages.subject: Setting factor levels for plot_coef()
parts:
Hi Juergen,

One more from me, I'm afraid. I have several site covariates that are categorical, and I'd like to manually set their levels so that my specified first factor is the median effect size to which all the others are compared, but I can't work out a streamlined way to do this.

e.g., I have a factor that is "basic lithology" with levels "Igneous", "Metamorphic", "Sedimentary". The analysis will automatically put them in this order when I run plot_coef(), even after I run a new model where I set these levels in the input data and datalist(). I'm replotting it all in ggplot so I've also tried releveling the plot_coef() output data (i.e., plot.coef$lithology$data$covariate) but all that does is change the position on the plot, so "Igneous" is still at y = 0.

Is there a way to somehow relevel factors in this process so that my selected first factor effect size is y = 0, or am I to be resigned to assigning dummy levels in my data that put everything in the order I want, and running the model again?

Thanks,
Jarrad

Hi Jarrad,
if this is still relevant, any chance you could provide a small reproducible example for illustration please? Maybe based on the vignette, which also has examples for working with factors. That would help a lot in understanding and fixing your issue.

Please also make sure it isn't yet answered in the vignette. From what I see the plot_* functions there always show a user-defined reference level of the categorical covariate first (the factor order was defined in the input data):
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr5.html#prepare-data
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr5.html#categorical-covariates

Thank you,
Jürgen
